name: lambda-hot
axis: closures: the per-call cost of a lambda in a hot loop, in four spellings (hand-inlined / named direct call / non-capturing lambda value / capturing closure)
notes: Four phases of n iterations each, all computing `(x + k) & 15` with a serial accumulator `acc = (acc + f(i)) & 1048575`. All values stay under 2^20, so no runtime has to reproduce another's integer-overflow rules, and the loop-carried dependency stops any of them vectorising it away. All four phases print the same number by construction (the offsets cancel over a whole period of 16) — that is the equivalence self-check. THE HEADLINE FINDING: per-phase VL timings at n=50,000,000 (prebuilt module, min-of-3) are 0.033s hand-inlined, 0.048s named direct call, 0.666s non-capturing lambda value, 0.670s capturing closure — a lambda held in a value costs ~13ns per call, 14x a direct call and 20x the inlined body. Rust and V8 both inline all four spellings, so both are effectively flat. `vl build -O` (plain binaryen -O, let alone -O3) collapses the lambda phases back to 0.033s, i.e. a 20x win from a pass VL does not run by default and `vl run` never runs. Totals at n=100,000,000: rust 0.134s, deno 0.263s, VL 2.243s (17x Rust, 8.5x deno), VL with the lambda contorted away (opt.vl) 0.300s, python(4M) 1.104s. Scale-verified 50M->100M: rust 2.22x, deno 1.99x, VL 2.38x, python 2M->4M 2.34x. Python's N is 1/25.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 114ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 6% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
